method.process: one Release app process with an empty isolated ANYWHERE_DATA_DIRECTORY
method.interaction: macOS accessibility UI through Computer Use
method.metrics: ps RSS, vmmap -summary Physical footprint, and heap --noContent class counts
method.privacy: clipboard recording remained disabled; no personal history, query, path or clipboard body was written to the evidence

web_document.fixture: locally built dev.example.text-pad version 1.1.1 from plugins/examples/web-text
web_document.process_shutdown: the captured stdout showed InAppWebView, FlutterWebViewController, channel delegate, message listener and WebMessage deallocation for the opened documents
web_document.functional_caveat: the Text Pad fixture displayed an INACTIVE notice while its page and editor still rendered; the run establishes memory and lifecycle behavior, not a complete Web plugin functional pass

observations: Opening either independent window added a second FlutterEngine, FlutterViewController and FlutterVSyncWaiter.
Closing either window returned those class counts to one; five open/close cycles did not leave additional engine or material objects.
Physical footprint remains affected by page residency, graphics backing stores and process history, so object release does not imply an immediate fixed RSS decrease.
A pair of Shelf open and closed samples returned both RSS and physical footprint to their pre-open values; Tasks retained a smaller residency high-water mark after close.
The measured incremental cost does not justify adopting an experimental shared multi-view engine before stable cross-platform APIs exist.
Opening a Web document created one WebContent, one GPU and one Networking helper; closing it removed WebContent and Networking and cleared WKWebView objects from the main process.
The WebKit GPU helper and shared process pool remained after close; five cycles did not create additional helpers, WKWebViews or message-handler objects.
Helper RSS is shown separately and must not be added directly to the main-process footprint as an exact whole-application total.
limitations: One Release process rather than three fresh processes per scenario.
The host was not otherwise under controlled memory pressure and background applications were not suspended.
The samples establish window lifetime and current cost, not a long-term leak bound or total application-memory decomposition.
No matched Flutter 3.47.8 process was measured.
Only one small local Web document was measured; large documents, multiple plugins, network resources, repeated reload and long-term helper retention remain unmeasured.
